ruling1_v1AuthoringGeneration.question: Is the v1 authoring shape a second authoring generation under ADR-SC-005 D-A? Execution-status normalisation ruled separately.

codesFate.LEGACY_AUTHORING: DELETED. Undeclared in OpenAPI, so no contract code list changes. A ui_tests row with authoring == null cannot be produced after the removal (the only create path stores authoring; D-B leaves no such rows). If one is met (a pre-D-B database or a test fixture that inserts SQL without authoring), every reader fails closed: guided start keeps its existing 409 RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE (GuidedSourceSnapshotRepository.java:31-34); GET/PUT /tests/{id} raise an internal integrity error (500, no resource detail, log testId only) AFTER the 403 authorization check; readiness reports UNLEARNED with firstChangedStepId null and execute refuses 409 LEARN_REQUIRED. No public code is minted for an unreachable state.

wordingConflictForPO.issue: AC-2/AC-6 say a client firstLearnStepId 'lower than the server's k is refused, higher is accepted (the author may choose to re-learn more, never less)'. Read as step position, 'lower' = earlier = MORE re-learning, which the parenthetical allows. Step IDs are UUIDs and have no order of their own.
wordingConflictForPO.rulingOnMeaning: The invariant governs: the client may move the learning start EARLIER (re-learn more) and may never move it LATER than the server's k (skip a changed or drifted step). Comparison is by the position of the step ID in the current draft authoring, never by UUID value.
wordingConflictForPO.action: @po clarifies AC-2/AC-6 wording before T5 writes the oracle (no meaning change intended). Not a T1 blocker.

startCommand.shape: commands#start gains two OPTIONAL fields: baseRevisionId (uuid) and firstLearnStepId (uuid). The server computes both; the session document records the server-resolved values; session-view echoes them.

refusals.case: firstLearnStepId positioned AFTER the server's k (skips a changed step)
firstLearnStepId not a step ID of the current draft (deleted or foreign)
baseRevisionId differs from the draft's confirmed revision, or is supplied when the draft is UNLEARNED

startCommand.accepted: firstLearnStepId at or before k; on READY (no edit) any step ID is accepted ('Learn again from step N', AC-5) and k := N. Omitted values mean 'use the server's'.
startCommand.whyReuse: AR-2 a: reuse a code wherever its meaning fits. REVISION_CONFLICT already means 'the client's view of the draft revision disagrees with the server' at the same place in start (GuidedSessionService.java:569-573, sourceRevision/configurationRevision). The common cause of a narrowed k is the same stale view (another save moved k earlier), and the FE remedy is identical: reload readiness and use the server's firstChangedStepId. A new code would add vocabulary with no new remedy. messageCode carries the sub-reason, as GuidedPolicyReason does (GuidedPolicyReason.java:17-19). error.schema code enum is unchanged.
startCommand.placementAndEffect: Checked in start's existing revision loop (after resolve and FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, before policies.activeForStart at :580 and csiBudget.admitStart at :582). Nothing is written: no session, no publication base, no budget charge.

changeDetectionHash_AC1.name: stepInputHash (per step; computed, not stored)
changeDetectionHash_AC1.composition: SHA-256, lowercase hex, over GuidedContracts.canonical (canonical-v1, GuidedContracts.java:406-489) of the closed object { domain: 'studio.step-input', version: 1, stepId, text (exact), context (the step's StepAuthoringContext as stored), references: [ ... ] } where references is the list, sorted by referenceId, of the declarations the step's text and step context reference: plain -> {referenceId, kind: 'plain', valueHash} (valueHash from AuthoringRevisionInputs.nonsecretReferencedValues), secret -> {referenceId, kind: 'secretRef', secretId}. Never a secret value, never a plain value in clear.
changeDetectionHash_AC1.testConfigHash: SHA-256 over canonical-v1 of { domain: 'studio.test-config', version: 1, environment, browser, viewport {width, height}, timeoutSeconds, waitStrategy, globalContextHash (AuthoringRevisionInputs.globalContext), globalReferences (same declaration form, for references used in globalContext) }. Any difference => k = 1.
changeDetectionHash_AC1.approvedOriginsNote: AC-1 lists 'approved origins' as test-level configuration, but after OBS-014 origins come from the governed policy (GuidedSessionService.java:580-581) and the trusted policy, not from the draft. Ruled: origins enter change detection only through the draft field that selects them (environment). A governance or TrustedPolicy change never changes k or readiness (consistent with AR-2 g: approving a governed version changes no verdict for existing revisions). An origin the session may no longer use surfaces at start as ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED (ruling3). @po: AC-1 wording note only.
changeDetectionHash_AC1.inputChain: inputChain_1 = SHA-256(canonical-v1 { domain: 'studio.step-chain', version: 1, stepId_1, stepInputHash_1, previous: testConfigHash }); inputChain_i = same with previous: inputChain_(i-1). Position is carried by the chain.
changeDetectionHash_AC1.k: k = the first position i (1-based) where the draft and the base revision differ in stepId or inputChain_i, or where one sequence ends. Rules this yields: edits, inserts, deletes and reorders count at the first affected position; multiple edits take the earliest; testConfigHash change => k = 1; identical sequences => READY; no confirmed revision => UNLEARNED. Pure tail deletion (draft is a strict prefix of the base) => k = the draft's last step (so firstChangedStepId stays a step of the draft and a session exists to publish the shorter revision); an empty draft cannot be learned (existing rule).
changeDetectionHash_AC1.baseSide: Computed from the base revision row alone (ui_test_revisions.authoring, authoring_revision_inputs, configuration, "references"; V12__tests_revisions.sql:5-35) with the same pure function as the draft side. STOP condition: if the referenced secret declarations (secretId) are not recoverable from the revision row, STOP and report to @architect; do not add a column or read the live draft's variables for the base side.

snapshotHash_stored.column: ui_test_revisions.step_snapshot_hashes: { stepId -> hex } (V15__publication.sql:496-503), one entry per authored step, enforced by the V15 guard (:505-541).
snapshotHash_stored.composition: snapshot_i = SHA-256(canonical-v1 { domain: 'studio.step-snapshot', version: 1, stepId, inputChain_i, learnedStepHash_i }).
snapshotHash_stored.learnedStepHash: learnedStepHash_i = SHA-256(canonical-v1 of the ordered list of the step's published learned-plan observedAction entries, each with admissionId removed, plus the binding definitions the step produces with session-bound fields removed). observedAction fields are coordinate, origin, locator, operation, admissionId, operationHash (learned-plan.schema.json definitions.observedAction). Exclusion is a closed DENY-list {admissionId and any receipt, evidence, timing, session or attempt identifier}: every other field, including fields added later, is committed by default, so a new session-bound field breaks reuse loudly (V15 guard raises) instead of weakening the commitment.
whyThisShape: AC-5: prefix steps reused from the base have byte-identical snapshot hashes (same stepId, same inputChain because positions 1..k-1 and config are unchanged, same learned content). The V15 guard then enforces reuse at the database: a reusedFrom entry is accepted only if the prior revision has the same hash for the same stepId (V15:528-535).

AC-6: steps k..n always differ from the base, even when their text is unchanged, because inputChain_k changed and the chain carries it forward. The oracle '1..3 equal, 4..10 differ' is deterministic, not an accident of new admission IDs.

AC-4(2): steps j..k-1 re-learned after prefix drift may hash equal to the base if re-learned identically; they carry NO step_reuse_provenance entry. 'Re-learned, not reused' is the absence of reusedFrom, never a forced hash difference.

Prefix admissions differ by design (AC-5: they come from this session's replay receipts), which is why admissionId is excluded per step and committed instead through admissionProvenanceHash over the merged admission list.
snapshotHash_stored.reusedFrom: step_reuse_provenance[stepId] = {revisionId: baseRevisionId, stepId} for every reused step, and only those (V15:524-535 already requires stepId = key and same test/CSI).
snapshotHash_stored.admissionProvenanceHash: Unchanged function (ObservedReferencePolicyDeriver.java:40, ordered ledger tuples {coordinate, admission, operationHash, scopeHash}) over THIS session's ledger, which holds both the prefix replay admissions and the suffix admissions (ruling3), ordered by coordinate.
snapshotHash_stored.verification: ObservedRevisionVerifier recomputes every snapshot hash from the revision's own authoring, inputs, configuration and plan and refuses a mismatch; stored values are never trusted. Java computes these hashes; the runner validator does not need to. publication-canonical-vectors.json gains vectors for the three domains (C-int) and a Java unit test pins them.
snapshotHash_stored.versionCost: Bumping any of the three domain versions makes every base recompute differ, so k = 1 for every test once. That is the accepted cost of a version bump.

ruling3_mixedModePolicy_R2.question: Which policy authorises prefix replay versus suffix learning in one session; which hash is recorded for the merged revision; the closed refusal when the frozen governed policy no longer allows a prefix origin.
ruling3_mixedModePolicy_R2.ruling: ONE policy for the whole mixed-mode session: the governed policy frozen at start (studio_guided_session_policies, V19__guided_governance.sql:108; frozen at GuidedSessionService.java:637) authorises BOTH the prefix replay and the suffix learning. The platform TrustedPolicy stays the ceiling (governed origins are a subset of trusted, re-checked at start with the existing RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE). Prefix replay in a learning session is NOT authorised through ObservedReplayAuthorizer / the replay grant; that path is ordinary /execute replay and stays unchanged (AR-2 g).
mechanism: Each prefix operation (content taken model-free from the base revision) is admitted through the session's existing action admission and ledger (GuidedActionLedger, policyDecisionHash from access.authorizeAction at GuidedSessionService.java:1243-1251) under the frozen governed policy. At-most-once, the ledger tuple and admissionProvenanceHash are then uniform across prefix and suffix.

Observation in the prefix uses the frozen governed applicationPolicy. This is structural, not a choice: the guided worker carries only the governed policy and rules: [] (ar-mounted-rules ruling), so TrustedPolicy.rules cannot be applied on the guided handle.

The model gateway is never reserved while state = REPLAYING_PREFIX (GuidedTranslationService refuses any reservation in that state). This is the structural guarantee behind 'gateway counters zero' (AC-3/AC-6).
Prefix actions count against the session's action counters and limits (existing BUDGET_EXCEEDED). Steps j..k-1 after drift charge the session model budget (AC-4(4)).

refusal.atStart: Before entering REPLAYING_PREFIX, the server checks that every origin the base revision's prefix (steps 1..k-1: observedAction.origin and the initialContext origin) needs is inside the frozen governed allowedOrigins. If not: 403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED, retryable false, messageCode PREFIX_ORIGIN_NOT_GOVERNED. The code already exists in error.schema.json and is used with 403 at GuidedDispatchService.java:213 and GuidedSourceReferenceValidator.java:147,188. Refused before any write: no session, no base, no budget charge (same as POLICY_NOT_APPROVED).
refusal.duringPrefix: An origin refusal during prefix replay (redirect or navigation outside the frozen governed origins) is a POLICY refusal, not target drift. Under AC-4 condition 1 it STOPS the run (FAILED, progress.errorCode ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED, as GuidedSessionService.java:530 already sets). It does not switch to learning, nothing is published, and no prefix action is repeated.
refusal.whyNotSwitchToLearning: Learning that step would be refused by the same governed origins, so switching would only spend model budget before failing.

ruling3_mixedModePolicy_R2.mergedRevisionRecord: The merged revision records exactly what a fully learned revision of THIS session records: the session's runAuthorizationHash, scopeHash (scope.approvedOrigins = frozen governed origins), and the referencePolicyHash / learnedPlanHash / admissionProvenanceHash / publicationEvidenceHash derived over the merged plan and this session's merged admissions (ObservedReferencePolicyDeriver.java:26-41). Governance provenance is this session's frozen (policy_id, policy_version, observation_policy_hash) via session_id. Nothing is carried from the base revision except the per-step snapshot hashes of reused steps and reusedFrom. There is no second 'prefix policy hash' and no dual-policy field. At later replay the merged revision behaves like any revision: currentPolicyHash = hash(TrustedPolicy(scope)) at replay time (ObservedReplayAuthorizer.java:92,120), unchanged.

alternativeRejected.option: Prefix under TrustedPolicy (as ordinary replay), suffix under the governed policy, both hashes recorded.
reasons: Re-learning would publish a NEW revision containing origins and reads that the current governance removed. Governance would be bypassed by editing a later step.
The guided worker has no TrustedPolicy.rules (ar-mounted-rules), so 'prefix under TrustedPolicy' would be partly fictional on the guided handle.
Two policy records per revision is exactly the unification problem the @pm follow-up owns; 015 must not absorb it (ruling request b).

ruling3_mixedModePolicy_R2.tradeOff: A NEEDS_RELEARN test whose prefix uses an origin that governance has since removed cannot be re-learned (ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED at start), while its old READY revision may still replay under TrustedPolicy until the edit. That is the R-2 interim state already disclosed (po-ar2-notes note 2 interimDisclosure); it fails closed for new publications.
ruling3_mixedModePolicy_R2.followUpDependency: None. This ruling confines the governed policy to the session and leaves replay authorisation untouched, so 015 does not wait for the @pm unification story.
